newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ag attache report on India soybeans, rice.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ag attache report on India soybeans, rice.

text.p: The following report by an agricultural attache at the American Embassy in New Delhi was made available in Washington on Thursday by the U.S. Agriculture Department. The report was dated July 25. Attache reports are not considered official USDA data.
SUMMARY: After a fairly good start to the monsoon, dry conditions have developed across key peanut, soybean, and rice producing areas over the past few weeks. END SUMMARY

Generally dry weather condition prevailed in most parts of central and western India during the week ending July 16. Only 16 out of the 35 weather subdivisions, received normal or above normal rainfall during the week.
Cumulative rainfall during June 1 to July 16 was normal or above normal in 26 out of 35 weather subdivisions.

The monsoon's performance was poor in several key agricultural areas during the past few weeks. If dry conditions continue, yields and area planted to key commodities like soybeans, peanuts, and rice could be affected.

PEANUTS: Heavy early season rains enabled planting in many peanut growing areas of Gujarat. However, conditions have subsequently been quite dry and the crop will need a second rain soon to keep yields on track. Dry conditions in Andhra Pradesh, a major producer of kharif peanuts, could also dampen yields.
SOYBEANS: In the major soybean growing regions of Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha in Maharashtra, rainfall since the beginning of the season has been consistent, but below normal.
However, conditions during the past two weeks have been quite dry and estimates of planted area in the 4.0 to 4.5 mha range are beginning to emerge; well below early season projections of 5.5 mha.

Farmers who planted early when rains were consistent have crops in the ground. However, rains have not developed for those who waited for better rainfall, and the window of opportunity for planting soybeans is about to close. Farmers who don't plant soybeans are likely to increase pulse or coarse grain area.

RICE: Coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh, which account for much of the state's rice production, have received significantly below normal rains so far. Rice transplanting in this largely rainfed area is progressing slowly and is reported to be well below the 2.3 mha which are normally planted to rice during the kharif season.
The state government is preparing a contingency plan to tackle the situation which involves distribution of seeds of short duration rice varieties along with pulses and coarse cereals.
